chunks: Al-'Ala' ibn Razin al-Qalla' narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about breastfeeding, and he said: Breastfeeding does not cause prohibition except what is sucked from a single breast for a year. This is a rare, unusual report, upon which action is withheld by consensus. And its ruling is that it is not objected against the numerous reports, for what we have clarified in other places.

key_terms.مَترُوكُ العَمَلِ بِهِ: Withheld action upon it (not acted upon)
key_terms.يُعتَرَضُ بِهِ: It is objected/used as a counter-argument

ai.seo_question: What is the specific condition for breastfeeding to cause prohibition according to this rare report from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this rare report from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), Al-'ala ibn Razin conveys a specific condition for breastfeeding prohibition: suckling from a single breast for a full year. Although considered 'shadh' (anomalous) and not the basis for general legal practice due to the consensus on more numerous reports, it remains a valid, non-overridable narration that illustrates the nuanced methodology of hadith evaluation in Shia jurisprudence.
